items.title: I hold my mother-in-law’s power of attorney. I’m also her executor and trustee. Do I have ultimate authority?
items.description: “There is a lot of legal and financial power in my hands.”

items.title: Treasury’s buyback blitz may end up driving bond yields higher, warns JPMorgan. Here’s its advice for investors.
items.description: Strategists Jay Barry and Jason Hunter are predicting fallout from the Treasury’s move that they see as not even needed.

items.title: A $420 camera for $10: China’s young consumers would rather rent than buy. It’s a problem for the government and the economy.
items.description: Young Chinese are renting cameras, drones and camping gear instead of buying them. It’s a clever way to save money — but also the latest challenge to Beijing’s effort to get consumers spending.

items.title: Walmart shares slide as U.S. sales hit by falling drug prices
items.description: The supermarket chain reported comparable U.S. sales growth of 2.6% in its second-quarter earnings, its lowest in over six years.

items.title: We’re in our 50s and have $1.5 million in traditional 401(k)s. Is it too early to start Roth conversions?
items.description: “The last adviser we worked with lost a significant portion of our portfolio.”

items.title: Oil prices jump after Trump declares economic war on Iran
items.description: President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that any country supporting Iran’s economy would face “tremendous economic consequences.”

items.title: AMD is betting on dirt-cheap AI chips, but financing them is a major question mark
items.description: AMD just acquired a company whose chip is fast, inexpensive and a total mystery for lenders.

items.title: Why Bessent’s Treasury operations have breathed life back into the gold trade
items.description: Gold is the reciprocal of the dollar and consensus among strategists is that Bessent’s yield curve control will have a detrimental impact on the U.S. currency

items.title: ‘There is considerable tension’: My grandmother, 99, wants to cut my mother out of her will. Should I intervene?
items.description: “Grandma feels that she was pressured by my mother into taking out a $50,000 HELOC.”
